What real problems add

topicin practice
random movesA move can land in more than one cell. Q then learns the average return.
huge state spacesA neural network replaces the table (DQN, Atari games).
SARSAUses the move it really takes next, not the best one. It learns the exploring policy.
policy gradientLearns the policy directly, without a Q table (REINFORCE, PPO).
ε scheduleε usually starts high and goes down, so the agent explores less later.
sparse rewardsWith one reward at the end, values take many episodes to spread back.

Terms

termmeaning
agentthe learner that picks the actions
state swhere the agent is: here, one cell
action aone move: up, right, down or left
reward rthe number the world returns after a move
episodeone walk from the start to an end cell
return Gthe sum of later rewards, each times γ per move of delay
Q(s, a)the expected return after action a in state s
γ (gamma)the discount: how much one move of delay costs
α (alpha)the learning rate: how far one update moves Q
ε (epsilon)how often the agent picks a random move
policy πthe rule that picks a move in each state
